rows.available: Assuming GI(s) and MN(s), every fixed affine-linear integer system of complexity at most s satisfies the generalized Hardy–Littlewood von Mangoldt asymptotic on convex bodies, with bounded size at the ambient scale. Pairwise nonparallel linear parts give complexity at most t−2 by singleton classes.
rows.needed: The surviving old41 affine lattice systems, with m<=41 nonconstant pairwise nonparallel forms in three variables, admit the weighted asymptotic for fixed coefficients and fixed cutoff L as X tends to infinity.
rows.derivation: Use the displayed local CRT parametrization and positive convex cone. Its m−1 singleton classes give complexity at most m−2<=39. Fix the lattice modulus, coefficients and cutoff L before increasing X; apply the theorem separately to finitely many surviving residue classes. Local-density lower bounds and removal of proper powers are the distinct local calculations at9516–9528.
premises: Exact affine parametrization and pairwise nonparallel forms from9460–9496.
Positive and quantitatively controlled local density from9497–9510 and9516–9528.
GI(39) and MN(39) from the next two relationships.
rows.boundary: No uniform error rate in varying L or varying coefficients. The lower-bound constant independent of L requires the separate displayed density argument; the theorem alone does not supply it.

rows.available: For a fixed Q-rational filtered nilmanifold of dimension m and degree d, every polynomial orbit and real1-bounded Lipschitz test has Möbius correlation bounded by a constant times Q to a fixed power times (1+LipF) times log(N)^(-A), uniformly in the orbit, for each fixed A>0. Constants depend on m,d,A and are ineffective.
rows.needed: MN(39) for the fixed nilsequence complexity entering the old41 finite-complexity prime theorem.
rows.derivation: Specialize to degree39 linear nilsequences and the rational bases supplied in the source remark; split real and imaginary parts when complex tests are used. Fixed geometry/Lipschitz data remain fixed before N increases.

Linear orbit is a polynomial orbit of the chosen degree filtration.
rows.boundary: This is Möbius orthogonality only, not a direct von Mangoldt or Gaussian weight estimate; GT Main Theorem supplies the separate transference step.

source.publication: Joseph H. Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, second edition2009

selected.scope: Four original old41 reduction inputs, kept separate from current Gaussian-pattern construction.

rows.available: For ell different from the characteristic, Hom(E1,E2) tensor Z_ell injects into Hom(T_ell E1,T_ell E2).
rows.needed: The rational centralizer of the defined order-four automorphism iota is exactly Q(i).
rows.derivation: Use ell=3 since the selected residue characteristic exceeds324. The iota action has minimal polynomial T²+1, irreducible over Q3. Its centralizer on the rank-two Tate space has dimension2. Injection bounds the rational centralizer by2, while its contained Q(i) already has dimension2.
rows.boundary: The actual good reduction, i in Fp and formula for iota are separate displayed local computations.

rows.available: The q-power Frobenius satisfies a monic integral quadratic polynomial in End(E).
rows.needed: The arithmetic p-power Frobenius, already in the rational centralizer Q(i), belongs to Z[i].
rows.derivation: Its coordinate action commutes with iota because i lies in Fp. The preceding rational-centralizer argument locates it in Q(i); the monic equation proves algebraic integrality, so it belongs to that field’s ring of integers.
rows.boundary: This does not assert all geometric endomorphisms belong to Q(i); only the centralizer and actual Frobenius do.

rows.locator: III Proposition8.6,p99; V Theorem2.3.1 and proof,p142
rows.available: On a prime-to-characteristic Tate module, determinant equals isogeny degree and trace equals1+degree(phi)−degree(1−phi). For q-power Frobenius the degree isq and degree(1−phi)=#E(Fq).
rows.needed: Writing Frobenius as a+bi gives p=a²+b² and the two opposite-twist orders p+1±2a.
rows.derivation: Over Q3(i), multiplication by a+bi has norm a²+b² and trace2a. Degree p and the point-count formula give the first order. The displayed opposite-squareclass twist relation negates the trace for the second.
rows.boundary: Opposite twists follow from product7 and the selected Legendre symbol; they are not an extra conclusion of the Tate determinant formula.

rows.available: For an elliptic curve over Fp, the point count differs from p+1 by at most2sqrt(p).
rows.needed: For the selected p>324, both orders are positive and below2p; their divisibility by4 excludes equality to oddp, so p divides neither.
rows.derivation: The inequalities p+1−2sqrt(p)>0 and p+1+2sqrt(p)<2p hold in this range. The complete rational two-torsion is the separate displayed reason for divisibility by4.
rows.boundary: The gcd2-part and odd-common-prime consequences are subsequent elementary arithmetic; no prime-pattern existence is supplied here.
